title: 03 · Config Server, Vault and MongoDB at startup, nothing at build time
question: The app connects to Config Server, Vault and MongoDB at startup; systems and credentials vary by environment and none of them is reachable at build time. Can a Spring AOT + AOT-cache image be built that way?

steps: Build the image with no network at all
Start Config Server, Vault and Mongo; give dev1 its credentials
Start dev1: config from Config Server, password from Vault, connect to Mongo
Rotate the password in Vault, restart: the same image picks it up
Break each dependency: startup refuses to run
preview.answer: Yes: the build needs no network; everything is fetched at startup, and a broken dependency stops startup.

answer.pass: Yes. Both build-time steps (Spring AOT processing inside mvn package, and the AOT-cache training run) ran with no network at all, skipping the Config Server and Vault imports. At startup the same image fetched its config from Config Server, its Mongo password from Vault and connected to Mongo. Rotating the password needed only a restart, not a rebuild, and an unreachable Config Server, an unreachable Vault or a bad Vault token each stopped startup.
answer.fail: Not as expected: at least one result differs from the known behaviour. See 'Unexpected results' for what differed and what to check.
answer.inconclusive: Some results couldn't be judged; rerun the example.

tested: A fresh (no-cache) image build, checking that the Maven build with Spring AOT and the AOT-cache training both ran under --network=none and skipped the remote imports.
This example's own Config Server, Vault and MongoDB (compose.yml) plus dev1's credentials: a Mongo user, its password in Vault, and a Vault token that can read only dev1's secrets.
Starting dev1 from that image: which Config Server file and Vault path it loaded, which database it used, and whether Mongo accepted the password.
Rotating the Mongo password in Vault and restarting the same image.
Three broken setups on one-off copies of dev1: Config Server unreachable, Vault unreachable, invalid Vault token.

build.maven-offline.label: mvn package incl. Spring AOT
build.maven-offline.why: Dependencies are downloaded in an earlier step; the build itself, including Spring AOT processing, runs offline with -o.
ifUnexpected: Read the build log in the evidence: a missing dependency means the go-offline step didn't fetch it (add dependency:resolve-plugins or the missing artifact).
Is Docker BuildKit enabled? RUN --network=none needs it.

build.imports-skipped.label: Config Server + Vault imports at build time
build.imports-skipped.why: build-time.yml points both clients at .invalid hosts with fail-fast off, so Spring AOT and the training run skip the imports instead of failing. Vault stays enabled, so the bean graph matches runtime.
ifUnexpected: Check that build-time.yml is passed via spring.config.additional-location (app/pom.xml process-aot and Dockerfile).
It must not be a profile file (application-build.yml): the imports run before profile files are read.

build.training-offline.label: JDK AOT-cache training run
build.training-offline.why: The training run starts the context (every bean is created) and exits before serving traffic; nothing in it needs a connection.
ifUnexpected: Read the build log in the evidence for the exception.
A bean that connects in its constructor or @PostConstruct would fail here; connect lazily instead.

started.label: started
started.why: The infra is up and dev1 has valid credentials.
ifUnexpected: Read the startup log in the evidence.
Is the infra healthy? docker compose ps (in examples/03-startup-connections)

start.aot.label: Spring AOT generated code in use
ifUnexpected: Check the image's ENTRYPOINT.

start.configserver.label: Config Server file for dev1
start.configserver.why: The configserver: import is resolved at every startup (AOT or not), using the profiles decided at startup (dev,dev1).
ifUnexpected: Check examples/03-startup-connections/config-repo/connections-app-dev1.yml exists and the Config Server is healthy.
Check the profiles in the startup log.

start.vault.label: Vault path for dev1
start.vault.why: The vault:// import is resolved at startup with dev1's token; its policy allows only dev1's paths.
ifUnexpected: Was bootstrap run for dev1? (examples/03-startup-connections/.secrets/dev1.env)
Vault runs in dev mode (in-memory): after a restart of Vault, run the bootstrap again.

start.mongo-db.label: Mongo database (from Config Server)
start.mongo-db.why: The database name comes from Config Server, not from the image.
ifUnexpected: Check config-repo/connections-app-dev1.yml in examples/03-startup-connections.

start.mongo-ping.label: Mongo accepted the password from Vault
start.mongo-ping.why: The password only exists in Vault (and Mongo); the app got it at startup.
ifUnexpected: Did the bootstrap's Mongo user and the Vault secret go out of sync? Rerun make -C examples/03-startup-connections start.

start.time.label: startup time against real Config Server, Vault and Mongo
start.time.why: Information only: includes the network round trips to Config Server and Vault.

rotation.changed.label: new password picked up after restart
rotation.changed.why: Secrets are read at startup, so a new value needs a restart, not a rebuild. (Refresh scope is off: it can't work with a bean graph fixed by AOT.)
ifUnexpected: Did the bootstrap rewrite secret/connections-app/dev1? Check its output in the terminal.
Was the container really recreated (docker compose up --force-recreate)?

rotation.ping.label: Mongo accepted the rotated password
rotation.ping.why: Mongo and Vault were updated together by the bootstrap; the restarted app used the new value.
ifUnexpected: Read the evidence (/info after rotation).

failfast.configserver.label: Config Server unreachable
failfast.configserver.why: fail-fast: true at runtime overrides 'optional:', so an environment can't silently start without its config.
ifUnexpected: If it started, fail-fast is off at runtime: check application.yml (spring.cloud.config.fail-fast) and that build-time.yml isn't loaded at runtime.

failfast.vault.label: Vault unreachable
failfast.vault.why: spring.cloud.vault.fail-fast: true at runtime, so missing secrets stop startup.
ifUnexpected: If it started, check spring.cloud.vault.fail-fast in application.yml.

failfast.token.label: invalid Vault token
failfast.token.why: Vault answers 403 and the app refuses to start, as it would with another environment's token.
ifUnexpected: If it started, the token wasn't used or Vault allowed it; check the evidence.

reproduce: make examples EX=03                                 # fresh build + full demo + report
make -C examples/03-startup-connections start       # infra + dev1 on :8301 (GET /info/connections)
make -C examples/03-startup-connections stop        # stop dev1 and its infra afterwards
